correctness.rationale: Under degree 2p+1 homogeneity with λ>0, f(θ)=⟨u,Q(u)⟩<0 and g(θ)=⟨Ju,Q(u)⟩>0, polar coordinates give dot r=λr+fr^(2p+1), dot θ=gr^(2p). Setting w=r^(2p) makes dw/dθ=a(θ)w+2pλ/g(θ), a=2pf/g<0. Its unique positive periodic solution w_*(θ)=2pλρ(θ)∫_(−∞)^θ [g(s)ρ(s)]^−1ds gives w=w_*+Cρ. C<0 reaches zero at finite backward angle but at t→−∞, C=0 is attracting cycle, C>0 has θ→−∞, w→∞ and finite backward physical time. For C>0, Δ(t)=∫_(−∞)^θ ds/[g(s)(w_*(s)+Cρ(s))]=K(θ)/(Cρ(θ))+O(ρ^−2), K=w_*/(2pλ), so Δr^(2p)=K(θ)+O(Δ). The conjugating clock Φ=log(K/ρ) has derivative 1/(gK)>0 and shift Φ(θ+2π)=Φ(θ)+Λ, yielding phase-resolved universal B(log(CΔ)) and complete accumulation interval. K constant iff f constant. Independently checked radial/angle identities and numerically showed Δr²−K→0 at θ−9,−14,−19 for the cubic witness; these tests support but do not prove all angular systems.
residual_risks: Strict angular drift g>0 and radial contraction f<0 are essential; neither equilibrium-polycycle nor vanishing-drift regimes are covered.
The guaranteed logarithmic period Λ need not be minimal when angular coefficients have smaller period.
